Critically, "(1.4)" never appears alone — the disputed sentence is "Edexcel IAL Business managing people (1.4)": exam board, qualification (IAL, explicitly not GCE), subject, and topic are all stated correctly immediately before the parenthetical. No reasonable reader would take the shorthand as an assertion that the official Pearson code is "1.4," any more than a textbook's own "Chapter 4" numbering claims to be a universal library classification. The parenthetical reads as this site's wayfinding index, exactly as "Section 1.4" does two lines later in the same file.

dismissed.quote: Spaced repetition practice for Edexcel IAL Economics and Business. Questions adapt to your knowledge using the SM-2 algorithm.
dismissed.whyDismissed: Independently verified every technical claim in the accusation against lib/spaced-repetition.js:37-87 and its call site (PracticeEngine.jsx:467) — all are accurate: binary isCorrect not 0-5 quality; flat +0.1/-0.2 ease deltas not the quality-weighted EF formula; 1-then-3-day early intervals not 1-then-6; a MAX_EASE=3.0 ceiling absent from canonical SM-2; a 10-minute retry on miss instead of a 1-day restart; and confidence defaulting to null at the only call site, making the confidence-modulation branches dead in production (matches F076). The reviewer read the source correctly.\n\nWhat keeps the copy defensible: (1) the disputed string is the page's <meta name=\"description\"> (SEO/share-snippet text), not the primary on-page copy — the actual visible headline on that page (lines 31-34) only says 'adapt to you using spaced repetition... come back sooner... space out over time,' which is fully accurate and undisputed; (2) the implementation is not an unrelated scheme wearing an SM-2 label — it uses SM-2's own signature constants (DEFAULT_EASE=2.5, MIN_EASE=1.3) and SM-2's defining mechanism (a repetitions counter gating early fixed intervals, then interval growth by multiplying by the ease factor), which is the same structural lineage software commonly ships under named-algorithm marketing (e.g. 'OAuth-based,' 'AES encryption,' Anki's own long-running 'SM-2' branding despite its documented deviations from the 1987 paper) without being deemed a false claim so long as the family/mechanism is genuinely present. The underlying sales promise — questions adapt to your knowledge, weak spots return sooner, mastered ones space out — is true and demonstrably delivered by buildQueue + computeNextReview regardless of the exact ease/interval constants used. That combination is a genuine, non-frivolous defense, so per the brief ('set defensible=false only if you cannot defend it') this clears the bar. A team that wants zero risk could still soften the meta description to 'an SM-2-inspired algorithm,' but that is precautionary polish, not a required correction of a false claim.

dismissed.quote: This question will come back — spaced repetition.
dismissed.whyDismissed:
I read both cited files directly.

QuestionCard.jsx:116 — the visible copy is: "This question will come back — spaced repetition." No timeframe is stated: it does not say "later in this session," "before you finish," or "today."

lib/spaced-repetition.js:98-144 (buildQueue) and PracticeEngine.jsx:433-444 confirm the reviewer's technical fact — the 20-item queue is built once at session start (handleStart) and never rebuilt mid-session, so a missed question cannot physically reappear before the current session ends.

But that only refutes a same-session reading, which the copy never asserts. What the copy is about — spaced repetition scheduling — genuinely happens and is genuinely correct: computeNextReview (spaced-repetition.js:60-67) resets a wrong answer's repetitions to 0 and sets intervalDays to TEN_MINUTES_IN_DAYS, i.e. nextReview = now + 10 minutes. That updated progress record is persisted (DB for logged-in users, localStorage otherwise — PracticeEngine.jsx ~447+). The next time buildQueue runs (the next practice session, which for an active student could be minutes or hours later), this item is now overdue and enters the `overdue` array with priority = time-since-due; overdue items are sorted most-overdue-first and get up to 70% of the new session's slots. There is no code path that drops or expires an overdue item — its priority (overdueMs) only grows the longer it's neglected, so across successive sessions it becomes progressively more likely to surface, not less. The mechanism the copy describes ("spaced repetition") is real, implemented correctly, and will in fact bring the question back — just possibly in a subsequent session rather than the current 20-question block.

Critically, "spaced repetition" is a specific, widely-recognized pedagogical term (Anki-style SRS) whose entire premise is that missed items return after a *spaced interval*, not immediately re-inserted into the same study block — that's what distinguishes it from simple immediate-retry/massed practice. By naming the mechanism explicitly, the copy signals to the reader that the return is scheduled, not instantaneous. A reader who knows what spaced repetition means would not expect the item back before finishing today's set.

Notably, the reviewer's own finding title hedges this: "'This question will come back' is false *within a session*" — a narrower claim than "false," and one the copy's text doesn't make. The reviewer is importing an implicit same-session promise that isn't in the string, then correctly observing the code doesn't deliver on that unstated promise. This is a case of the accusation reading in a temporal guarantee the copy doesn't contain, rather than the copy asserting something false.

I don't think this is quite "unsubstantiated marketing puffery" either — it's a specific, true technical claim about the app's actual scheduling algorithm, verified by reading the algorithm itself.

One caveat worth flagging separately (not a copy defect): the 10-minute interval constant and the "come back sooner" comment suggest the original engineering intent may have been same-session reappearance, and the queue-never-rebuilds behavior may be a genuine product/UX gap worth fixing (dynamically re-inserting due items into the live queue). But that's a product/engineering ticket, not evidence the marketing copy is false.

16. **Rate limits vs "ask anything" claims.** `app/api/chat/route.js:9-10` sets `DAILY_LIMIT = 30` and it is applied *after* the premium check (`:62-68`), so paying users are capped at 30 tutor messages/day. Uncited claims that this contradicts: `app/economics/page.js:316` and `:389` *"Ask any Economics question"*, `app/business/page.js:311` and `:384` *"Ask any Business question"*, `app/upgrade/page.js:21` *"AI tutor — Answers in exam language, any hour of the night"*. Only the parallel 50/day cap on `/written-practice` was caught.
17. **The two `/upgrade` Pro bullets nobody tested.** `app/upgrade/page.js:20` *"Quizzes with marking — Examiner-style feedback, not just right or wrong"* — `components/QuizTab.jsx` is multiple choice: it compares `answers[i] === q.correctIndex` and prints a static `q.explanation` string (`:125-144`). There is no marking and no examiner-style feedback. `:16` *"Evaluation chains — The 20-mark technique, built step by step"* — `components/ExtrasTab.jsx` renders two flat arrays (`chains`, `evaluation`) and shows "coming soon" when both are empty; check how many sections actually have them.
18. **Traction / social-proof claims.** `app/economics/page.js:434`: *"our content… is used by students in South Korea, Hong Kong, Malaysia, Singapore, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and across the Middle East."* An unevidenced user-base claim in indexed prose. The same paragraph also asserts *"adaptive flashcards with spaced repetition"* and model answers as part of the free offer. Nothing else on the site claims student numbers, ratings, testimonials or "trusted by" — `aggregateRating`/`reviewCount`/`testimonial` return zero hits, so that class is genuinely clean.
19. **Competitor comparison.** `app/economics/page.js:434` opens *"Unlike generic revision sites…"* — the only competitor-comparison claim on the site and unverified. Related: `app/economics/page.js:141` and `app/business/page.js:136` FAQ JSON-LD assert what the UK domestic A-Level is and is not; these are rich-result answers about a third party's qualification.
20. **Pearson/Edexcel proximity.** `app/layout.js:64` publishes an `EducationalOrganization` with an `offers` object and no disclaimer, and every page title leads with "Edexcel IAL". There is no "not affiliated with or endorsed by Pearson" statement anywhere in `app/` or `components/`. Worth a decision as a class, not 182 line fixes.
21. **Exam-table rows on the four Business unit pages.** The Economics unit pages were fully audited (duration, "% of A-Level", sections) but on Business only the "choose 1 of 2" row and the mark pills were. Still unchecked: `app/business/unit-1/page.js:134`, `unit-2:133`, `unit-3:141`, `unit-4:126` all label the row **"% of A-Level"** — the identical UK-GCE framing that produced findings on all four Economics pages — plus the Duration and Total marks rows (`unit-1:132-133` = 2 hours / 80 marks).
22. **The features strip on all eight unit pages** (`grep` shows 2 hits per file in `app/business/unit-{1..4}` and `app/economics/unit-{1..4}`): *"Spaced repetition — Adaptive flashcard algorithm"* and *"Progress tracking — Mastery across all spec points"*. Both are claims the audit already proved false elsewhere (`upgrade/page.js:19`; `/progress` ignores Learn Mode, Quiz and Flashcards), but these 16 lines were never cited.
23. **The two hub "What's included" cards nobody cited.** `app/economics/page.js:304` / `app/business/page.js:299`: *"Spaced repetition that learns from you — topics you struggle with come back sooner, mastered ones space out automatically"*, tagged **Premium**. That describes `/flashcards-practice` (free, SM-2), not the premium Flashcards tab, which stores only a got-it flag.
24. **Nine Economics + two Business section model-answer pages with zero findings**, all using the same "Covers A, B and C" pattern that produced confirmed failures on seven sibling pages: `app/economics/{introductory-concepts,demand,supply,market-failure,aggregate-demand,aggregate-supply,national-income,economic-growth,macroeconomic-policies}-model-answers/page.js` and `app/business/{raising-finance,marketing-mix}-model-answers/page.js` (the latter two were cited only for the GCE spec number, not for topic coverage). Each has 2-3 answers behind a 3-4 topic promise; e.g. `introductory-concepts` promises "the basic economic problem" and that phrase does not appear in either answer.

## (c) Confirmed claims that are live in more than one place

25. **"£1 first month" — cited once (`app/upgrade/page.js:77`), live in 18 files / ~29 occurrences**: `app/upgrade/page.js` ×6 (including the page `title` at :4, `description` at :5 and both openGraph fields at :7-8 — four copies in metadata alone), `components/PaywallOverlay.jsx` ×7, `components/StudyApp.jsx` ×2, `components/SettingsPage.jsx` ×1, plus `economics/page.js`, `business/page.js`, all eight unit pages and the three Economics pillar pages. Fixing line 77 leaves the misleading promise on every paywall a returning subscriber sees.
26. **"Practice questions … unlock with Pro" — cited on the four Economics unit pages only.** The identical sentence is on `app/business/unit-1/page.js:161`, `unit-2:160`, `unit-3:168`, `unit-4:153`. Practice is in `FREE_TABS`, so the Business pages tell a parent to pay for a free feature too.
27. **GCE section numbering is in the data layer, not just the copy.** `data/modelAnswersData.js` stores `sectionNumber: '1.1' … '2.5'` for all 20 Business answers, `SECTION_MODEL_ANSWERS_FAQ` is keyed by those same numbers, and `components/SectionModelAnswersPage.jsx:15-19` filters on `sectionNumber`. Two consequences: (i) changing the visible "(1.1)" text without changing the data leaves the numbers live, because `components/ModelAnswersPage.jsx:352` renders `Unit {unit} · {sectionNumber} {sectionTitle}` on every answer card — on `/model-answers` and on each section page; (ii) changing the data without changing the page props and the FAQ keys makes those pages render zero answers.
28. **Off-spec vocabulary is duplicated well beyond the marketing copy.** "merit good" also appears in `data/modelAnswersData.js`, `data/modelAnswersExpansion.js`, `seed/extras-economics.mjs`, `seed/economics-flashcards.mjs`, `seed/economics-practice-unit1.mjs`, `components/TutorTab.jsx:33` (a suggested tutor prompt: *"What is the difference between merit and demerit goods?"*) and `app/economics/market-failure-model-answers/page.js:5` — a page with no findings at all. Fixing the pillar page leaves the flashcards, quiz, model answers and tutor prompts teaching the same non-IAL term.

## One likely false positive in the confirmed set

29. **`app/economics/market-failure/page.js:523` — "Fully worked 8- and 20-mark answers"** is recorded as false on the grounds that 1.3.5 has only a 4-mark Explain. It does not: importing the data gives three Economics 1.3.5 answers — `neg-externality-4` (4m Explain), `negative-externality-tax-8` (8m Analyse) and `market-failure-government-intervention-20` (20m Evaluate) — and `SectionModelAnswersPage` filters on exactly `sectionNumber === '1.3.5' && subject === 'economics'`. Re-verify before shipping a rewrite of correct copy.
